The CONTROL device formulation employs m-Br-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL as a key additive in the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ perovskite precursor solution, alongside MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and SAM 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL). While m-Br-PEACl contributes to surface smoothing, its meta-bromine substitution introduces steric hindrance that limits effective passivation of undercoordinated Pb²⁺ defects at grain boundaries and interfaces. This results in persistent non-radiative recombination, evidenced by the moderate fill factor (81.26%) and open-circuit voltage (1.179 V) despite a high short-circuit current density (26.24 mA/cm²). The bromine atom also promotes halide ion migration under operational stress, accelerating phase segregation and voltage losses, which caps Voc and FF improvements. Additionally, the meta-position reduces molecular packing efficiency on the perovskite surface, weakening interfacial energy level alignment and charge extraction.  

Replacing m-Br-PEACl with p-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL addresses these limitations through para-fluorine substitution. The fluorine atom’s strong electron-withdrawing nature enhances binding affinity to Pb²⁺ defects, significantly suppressing deep-level trap states and non-radiative recombination. This improves interfacial energy level alignment, reducing voltage losses and boosting charge carrier lifetime. The para-configuration enables optimal molecular orientation, minimizing steric effects and promoting uniform passivation across grain boundaries. Consequently, ion migration is inhibited, stabilizing the perovskite lattice against phase segregation and reducing hysteresis. While the fluorine substitution slightly widens the bandgap, marginally lowering light absorption, the dominant effect is a substantial reduction in recombination losses. This trade-off is favorable: the Voc and FF gains outweigh the minor Jsc reduction, as recombination was the primary bottleneck in the CONTROL device.  

The optimized formulation maintains all other components unchanged—perovskite stoichiometry (Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃, 1.65 mol/L), SAM (4,4,4-NA, 0.5 mg/mL), MACl (15.0 mg/mL), and PDADI passivation (0.5 mg/mL)—to isolate the impact of the PEACl variant. Performance improvements manifest as a Voc between 1.17 and 1.21 V, Jsc between 25.39 and 25.79 mA/cm², FF between 83.9% and 85.9%, and PCE between 24.83% and 26.71%. The elevated FF and Voc directly stem from reduced recombination and improved interfacial kinetics, while the slight Jsc decrease reflects the bandgap trade-off, which is acceptable given the net PCE gain.
